title: llm 0.37
summary_raw: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. title: Huawei tells customers to find their own AI chip memory, effectively outsourcing procurement to the black market
summary_raw: Huawei is telling customers to source the high-performance memory for its AI chips on their own, pushing them onto the black market. Smugglers are exploiting a loophole in U.S. export rules by bundling HBM with low-end processors, shipping them through Hong Kong, and separating the chips on site. Prices for smuggled HBM3E memory have surged to around $4,000 per unit in just one year. title: One brutal Minecraft night scared 50 AI agents into inventing chicken handoff protocols, a Fertilizer Officer, and fishing shifts
summary_raw: In experiments by Y Combinator Labs and Olam Labs, OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol model showed two very different sides. When 50 agents were tasked with peaceful civilization-building in Minecraft, they froze up in absurd bureaucracy. Simulations like these are meant to serve as an early warning system before AI swarms act unpredictably in real-world systems. title: The $1B Company Fixing AI’s Software Bottleneck
summary_raw: Blacksmith (YC W24) is building a faster cloud for continuous integration (CI), helping developers test and ship code as AI coding tools generate more of it. As software production accelerates, testing and validation are becoming the new bottleneck. That shift has helped Blacksmith grow 20x over the last year, and the company recently raised a $66 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation. The founders started as outsiders to DevOps and built their first infrastructure using the same high-performance CPUs found in gaming PCs, renting servers originally designed for Minecraft and Call of Duty.
